title: Grand Aurora: Failure & Recovery
description: AZ A/B are illustrative, not deployable AZ identifiers. ALB nodes require enabled subnet mappings in both AZs; its subnet mappings and VPC Link ingress are aggregated. Task and DB security groups need explicit rules. Aurora compute instances use DB subnets; the shared cluster volume is regional managed infrastructure with storage across three AZs. A reader is not a separately writable replica. The recovery arrow denotes role promotion, not reverse replication. Aurora Global Database requires supported versions/regions and asynchronously replicates storage. Standby activation requires fencing the previous writer, database promotion and traffic/credential changes. Lag, loss and manual recovery decisions remain possible. Backups assume a supported encrypted cross-account copy configuration, dedicated roles, KMS grants and restore tests. A backup is not a hot replica. No RTO/RPO, zero-loss failover or production readiness is claimed. This view expands one pooled cell, not every enterprise deployment.

edges.meaning: ALB spans enabled AZ subnets and sends healthy requests to private tasks A.
Independent task replicas in another AZ; security groups constrain ingress.
Booking transactions use the cluster writer endpoint, not the reader endpoint.
Tasks in AZ B can reach the same writer through permitted intra-VPC traffic.
Aurora writer persists to its distributed cluster volume; storage spans three AZs independently of app placement.
Reader shares cluster storage and applies updates; not a second independent writable database.
Eligible reader promotion changes the writer role after failure; this is a recovery transition, not a reverse data stream.
Assumed Aurora Global Database asynchronously replicates to the supported recovery region; lag and data loss are possible.
Standby activation follows fencing of the old writer and explicit database promotion.
Scheduled AWS Backup cross-account copy needs supported resources, organization configuration, backup role and KMS policies.
